'''''The Phoenician Scheme''''' is a 2025 [[black comedy]] [[espionage thriller]] film written, produced, and directed by [[Wes Anderson]] from a story he conceived with [[Roman Coppola]]. The film features an [[ensemble cast]] that includes [[Benicio del Toro]], [[Mia Threapleton]], [[Michael Cera]], [[Riz Ahmed]], [[Tom Hanks]], [[Bryan Cranston]], [[Mathieu Amalric]], [[Richard Ayoade]], [[Jeffrey Wright]], [[Scarlett Johansson]], [[Benedict Cumberbatch]], [[Rupert Friend]], [[Hope Davis]], [[F. Murray Abraham]], [[Charlotte Gainsbourg]], [[Willem Dafoe]], and [[Bill Murray]].<!--This is the OFFICIAL cast listing order from the poster.--> It tells the story of a ruthless businessman (del Toro) as he seeks to reconcile with his estranged daughter (Threapleton) and complete an ambitious infrastructure project in [[Phoenicia]]. The film was produced internationally between the United States and Germany by Anderson's company American Empirical Pictures and [[Steven Rales]]'s company [[Indian Paintbrush (company)|Indian Paintbrush]].

Anderson talked about the film in June 2023 while promoting ''[[Asteroid City]]''; he said it had already been written before the [[2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 WGA strike]] began. That September, he revealed that del Toro and Cera were planned to join the cast, and he hoped to begin filming soon after the [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike]] ended. The rest of the cast signed on between January and June 2024. Filming took place at [[Babelsberg Studio]] in Germany, between March and June 2024, with cinematographer [[Bruno Delbonnel]]. Frequent Anderson collaborator [[Alexandre Desplat]] returned to compose the score.

''The Phoenician Scheme'' had its world premiere in the main competition of the [[2025 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] on May 18, 2025,<ref name="Screenings Guide" /> and was released theatrically in Germany by [[Universal Pictures]] on May 29, 2025, and in the United States by [[Focus Features]] on May 30, 2025. The film received generally positive reviews.

== Plot ==
In 1950, [[Statelessness|stateless]] arms dealer and industrialist Anatole "Zsa-Zsa" Korda narrowly survives a sixth assassination attempt. Knowing he cannot run forever, Korda tries to mend his relationship with his only daughter, Catholic [[Novitiate|novice]] Sister Liesl, and enrolls her in his ambitious scheme to overhaul the infrastructure of [[Phoenicia]] using slave labor. A consortium of governments around the world, seeking to curb Korda's tendency to manipulate global conflict and peace to suit his own interests, conspires to drive up the price of building materials, jeopardizing the project's financing and threatening to bankrupt Korda.

With Liesl and Bjørn, a Norwegian [[Entomology|entomologist]] and administrative assistant in tow, Korda travels to meet and attempt to swindle his major partners. He deceitfully asks Californians Leland and Reagan to sign a contract increasing their investment, blackmails French gangster Marseille Bob, and threatens East Coast businessman Marty with a [[suicide bombing]]. The partners are enraged but all ultimately agree to contribute, though they only manage to cover 50% of the budget shortfall.

During the trip, Korda has several visions of the afterlife. A divine court judges his worthiness to enter Heaven, and Liesl's deceased mother reveals that he is not Liesl's father. He realizes that all he had to offer his family was money, not love. In addition, he confesses to Liesl his guilt in contributing to the death of her mother, who was murdered by his estranged half-brother Nubar, with whom she was having an affair. Liesl is outraged at her father's amorality but agrees to continue helping him, hoping that he might change his ways and Nubar would face justice.

In a last-ditch attempt to avoid asking Nubar for help, Korda offers to marry his cousin Hilda, an heiress to the Korda armaments fortune. She accepts his proposal but refuses to increase her investment. Korda's plane is destroyed by saboteurs on the way home, and in the aftermath Bjørn is unmasked as a spy working for the government consortium. However, having fallen in love with Liesl, Bjørn agrees to switch sides. Liesl resolves to return to the convent, but her [[mother superior]] dismisses her, explaining that she is not cut out for religious life.

Korda, Liesl, and Bjørn finally meet with Nubar, who denies being Liesl's real father and announces that he is withdrawing his entire investment. Having failed to meet the budget shortfall, Korda throws his entire personal fortune into the Phoenician scheme, reasoning that finishing a worthy project will give his life meaning. He also decides to pay his workers and convert to Catholicism. The investors gather at the Desert Oasis Palace hotel to witness a presentation of the scheme. Nubar returns, reveals that he was behind the attempts on Korda's life over a long-held grudge, and tries to personally murder Korda. Korda fatally wounds him before he blows himself up with a grenade.

Liesl reconciles with a bankrupted Korda and agrees to accept him as her father. The two retire to a simpler life running a small bistro. Hilda has her brief marriage to Korda annulled and gives back her wedding ring. Korda loans the ring to Bjørn, who proposes to Liesl; she accepts. At the end of the working day, Liesl and Korda play cards together as a family.

== Production ==
=== Development ===
Anderson decided to write a story about the Near East after the death of his father-in-law, Lebanese engineer Fouad Malouf, to whom the film is dedicated. Anderson remembered Malouf as "an amazing kind of larger-than-life figure ... wise and very intelligent, but a little bit scary."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Galuppo |first=Mia |date=2025-05-13 |title=Wes Anderson on 'The Phoenician Scheme,' His Cannes Party Bus and Why You Should Always See His Movies Twice |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/wes-anderson-interview-the-phoenicians-scheme-1236209089/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=June 10, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250610155743/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/wes-anderson-interview-the-phoenicians-scheme-1236209089/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He wanted to make a movie where a father "realizes that actually his giant business plan is a ritual, a scheme to get [his daughter]."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Puchko |first=Kristy |date=2025-06-06 |title=Wes Anderson on the personal inspirations for 'The Phoenician Scheme' |url=https://mashable.com/article/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-interview |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Mashable |language=en |archive-date=June 8, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250608163541/https://mashable.com/article/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-interview |url-status=live }}</ref> When Malouf's health began failing, he showed Anderson's wife a series of shoeboxes he had used to organize his files and memories. Anderson adapted the shoeboxes for his film, where Zsa-Zsa Korda uses shoeboxes to organize his business plans.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Adams |first=Sam |date=2025-06-06 |title=In Wes Anderson's New Movie, He Examines His Own Limitations |url=https://slate.com/culture/2025/06/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-new-movie-christianity.html |access-date=2025-06-09 |work=Slate |language=en-US |issn=1091-2339 |archive-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607103340/https://slate.com/culture/2025/06/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-new-movie-christianity.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

For the character of Zsa-Zsa, Anderson drew on real-life industrialists of the period, saying that he wanted a character who could have "walked out of an [[Michelangelo Antonioni|Antonioni]] movie with his sunglasses."<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Shafer |first=Ellise |date=2025-05-30 |title=Benicio del Toro Calls 'The Phoenician Scheme' Role a 'Gift' as Wes Anderson Says 'He Was the Only One I Ever Considered': 'Actors Dream of Moments Like This' |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/global/benicio-del-toro-wes-anderson-the-phoenician-scheme-1236410776/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> Zsa-Zsa's lavish palazzo, fondness for art collecting, and nickname "Mr. Five Percent", are borrowed from [[Armenians|Armenian]] oil magnate [[Calouste Gulbenkian]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Greenberger |first=Alex |date=2025-05-30 |title=Wes Anderson's 'The Phoenician Scheme' Features a Real Renoir and a Salient Spoof of Art Collecting |url=https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-renoir-art-collecting-1234743890/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=ARTnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In addition, the name, look, and British manner of Zsa-Zsa's brother Nubar are borrowed from Gulbenkian's son [[Nubar Gulbenkian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bradshaw |first=Nick |date=2025-05-23 |title=The Phoenician Scheme review |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/reviews/phoenician-scheme-benicio-del-toro-steals-show-death-defying-tycoon-wes-andersons-latest-caper |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=BFI |language=en}}</ref> (Another influence for Nubar may be the title character of the 1955 film ''[[Mr. Arkadin]]''.)<ref name=":4">{{Cite magazine |last=Brody |first=Richard |date=2025-05-29 |title=Is "The Phoenician Scheme" Wes Anderson's Most Emotional Film? |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2025/06/09/the-phoenician-scheme-movie-review |access-date=2025-06-09 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref> Anderson mentioned businessmen [[Aristotle Onassis]], [[Stavros Niarchos]], [[Gianni Agnelli]], and [[William Randolph Hearst]] as additional influences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wallace |first=Rachel |date=2025-05-21 |title=An Exclusive Look Inside 'The Phoenician Scheme,' Wes Anderson's Zany New Film |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/gallery/see-inside-the-phoenician-scheme-wes-andersons-zany-new-film |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Architectural Digest |language=en-US |archive-date=June 9, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250609025701/https://www.architecturaldigest.com/gallery/see-inside-the-phoenician-scheme-wes-andersons-zany-new-film |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":3" /> The mechanical diorama that features at the climax of the film references ''[[The Rules of the Game]]'' (1939), another film lampooning the rich and marking the end of an era for the European elite.<ref name=":4" />

Anderson chose to focus the film on religion, while admitting that he personally believed only "roughly" in God.<ref name=":2" /> He explained that his high school had [[Episcopal Church (United States)|Episcopal]] influences and that "if you grow up being given this religion, it's sort of always there".<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Shaffer |first=Marshall |date=2025-05-30 |title=Wes Anderson and Michael Cera on 'The Phoenician Scheme' |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/wes-anderson-michael-cera-interview-the-phoenician-scheme/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Slant Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> The film's afterlife sequences have been compared to [[Powell and Pressburger]]'s film ''[[A Matter of Life and Death (1946 film)|A Matter of Life and Death]]'' (1946),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aftab |first=Kaleem |date=2025-05-16 |title=Review: The Phoenician Scheme |url=https://www.timeout.com/movies/the-phoenician-scheme-review-2025 |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=Time Out |archive-date=May 22, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522203210/https://www.timeout.com/movies/the-phoenician-scheme-review-2025 |url-status=live }}</ref> and the surname Korda may be a reference to the Hungarian-British filmmaker [[Alexander Korda]], who produced many Powell and Pressburger films, though not ''A Matter of Life and Death'' itself.<ref name=":2" /> The film's religious sequences were also inspired by [[Luis Buñuel]].<ref name=":6" />

Anderson's longtime collaborating producer [[Steven Rales]] and his company [[Indian Paintbrush (company)|Indian Paintbrush]] produced the film.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Matt |first1=Grobar |date=March 11, 2024 |title=Wes Anderson Shares Why He Was Absent From Oscars & What He Would've Said Following Win For Netflix Short ''The Wonderful Story Of Henry Sugar'' |url=https://deadline.com/2024/03/wes-anderson-talks-oscars-absence-speech-he-wouldve-given-1235855245/ |access-date=14 March 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=March 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314174721/https://deadline.com/2024/03/wes-anderson-talks-oscars-absence-speech-he-wouldve-given-1235855245/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Alexandre Desplat]] returned to compose the score, his seventh collaboration with Anderson.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 11, 2025 |title=Alexandre Desplat Scoring Wes Anderson's ''The Phoenician Scheme'' |url=https://filmmusicreporter.com/2025/02/11/alexandre-desplat-scoring-wes-andersons-the-phoenician-scheme/ |access-date=February 11, 2025 |website=Film Music Reporter}}</ref>

''[[Screen Rant]]'' reported that [[F. Murray Abraham]] joined the cast.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/the-phoenician-scheme-movie-benicio-del-toro-mia-theapleton-image/ |title=Exclusive Phoenician Scheme Image Is Wes Anderson's Latest Fraught Father-Child Relationship In A Nutshell |last=Gearan |first=Hannah |date=May 7, 2024 |website=[[Screen Rant]] |access-date=May 10, 2025 |archive-date=May 10, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250510100347/https://screenrant.com/the-phoenician-scheme-movie-benicio-del-toro-mia-theapleton-image/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The rest of the cast was announced on June 6, 2024, including [[Tom Hanks]], [[Benedict Cumberbatch]], [[Scarlett Johansson]], [[Willem Dafoe]], [[Bryan Cranston]], [[Mia Threapleton]], [[Tonio Arango]], Imke Büchel, Imad Mardnli, Jaime Ferkic, Antonia Desplat, Aysha Samuel, and Sabine Hollweck.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thefilmstage.com/wes-andersons-the-phoenician-scheme-adds-scarlett-johansson-tom-hanks-willem-dafoe-benedict-cumberbatch-charlotte-gainsbourg-more/ |title=Wes Anderson's The Phoenician Scheme Adds Scarlett Johansson, Tom Hanks, Willem Dafoe, Benedict Cumberbatch, Charlotte Gainsbourg & More |last=Pearce |first=Leonard |date=June 6, 2024 |website=The Film Stage |access-date=June 6, 2024 |archive-date=September 30, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240930011738/https://thefilmstage.com/wes-andersons-the-phoenician-scheme-adds-scarlett-johansson-tom-hanks-willem-dafoe-benedict-cumberbatch-charlotte-gainsbourg-more/ |url-status=live }}</ref> With the announcement of the release date, it was revealed in February 2025 that [[Mathieu Amalric]] and [[Jeffrey Wright]] were part of the cast.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Wes Anderson's Next Film 'The Phoenician Scheme' Gets May Release Date, Focus Features to Distribute|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|first=Brent|last=Lang|date=11 February 2025|access-date=11 February 2025|url=https://variety.com/2025/film/news/wes-anderson-next-film-phoenician-scheme-release-date-focus-features-1236303296/}}</ref>

Threapleton had been a fan of Anderson since she watched ''[[Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)|Fantastic Mr. Fox]]'' (2009) when she was eight or nine years old.<ref name="rollingstone"/> When she was thirteen, she wrote on her journal, "Watching ''[[Moonrise Kingdom]]'' (2012) again, bloody love this film. Would love to work with Wes Anderson one day."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seth |first=Radhika |date=20 May 2025 |title=The Phoenicin Scheme's Mia Threapleton on Crying During Her Standing Ovation and Mom Kate Winslet's Cannes Advice |url=https://www.vogue.com/article/mia-threapleton-the-phoenician-scheme-cannes-review |website=[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]}}</ref> She landed the role of Sister Liesl after a long audition process that began in May 2023, when she sent Anderson a self-shot audition tape without knowing anything about the character that she would portray. Her tape stood out among over a thousand of auditions that Anderson had watched at that point, "She just seemed like she was in a documentary about the scene. I could see her thoughts. You could tell she was really listening, reacting, thinking about what was happening in front of her. Which isn't always the case", he said. Anderson then asked her to meet with him in London and later for a reading and two-day screen test with del Toro. Both Anderson and del Toro (who plays her character's father in the film) agreed that she should be cast for the role.<ref name="rollingstone">{{Cite magazine |last=Fear |first=David |date=24 May 2023 |title=Mia Threapleton Idolized Wes Anderson. Then She Became the Breakout Star of His New Movie |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/mia-threapleton-wes-anderson-phoenician-scheme-interview-1235338905/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=June 1, 2025 |archive-date=June 1, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250601033445/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-features/mia-threapleton-wes-anderson-phoenician-scheme-interview-1235338905/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Del Toro, who endorsed Threapleton after their first reading together,<ref name="rollingstone"/> said, "When she walked out, I remember telling Wes, 'I think she can go toe to toe; she might be short, but she's terrific'".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Emma |date=20 May 2025 |title='She might be short, but she's terrific': The sensational break-out star of The Phoenician Scheme |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20250521-the-sensational-break-out-star-of-the-phoenician-scheme |website=[[BBC News]] |access-date=June 1, 2025 |archive-date=May 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524032948/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20250521-the-sensational-break-out-star-of-the-phoenician-scheme |url-status=live }}</ref> Anderson said that Threapleton already had the role five minutes into the second day of screen test. "And when you saw her read against Benicio... I mean, he's a very imposing figure, and about a foot-and-a-half taller than Mia, for one thing. But if you were to say who seemed to have the power in the relationship in the scenes, you would tend to lean towards the nun."<ref name="rollingstone"/> Anderson said he only discovered that Threapleton is [[Kate Winslet]]'s daughter after he had watched her audition video a few times and then looked her up to check her previous work.<ref name="rollingstone"/>

To prepare for her role as a nun, Threapleton, who is not Catholic, talked to a [[Deacon]] and studied [[Catholicism]] in Rome with the help of the film's costume designer, [[Milena Canonero]], who is based out of Rome.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 29, 2025 |title=Mia Threapleton on Preparing for Role in 'The Phoenician Scheme' |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0eGk8D5AjR4&t=158s |work=[[Today (American TV program)|Today Show]] |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

=== Filming ===
[[Principal photography]] began on March 12, 2024, at [[Babelsberg Studio]] in Germany, and wrapped on June 3 of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Calnan |first=Ellie |date=March 12, 2024 |title=Wes Anderson shooting new film ''The Phoenician Scheme'' in Germany |url=https://www.kftv.com/news/2024/03/12/wes-anderson-new-film-the-phoenician-scheme-shooting-germany |access-date=March 12, 2024 |website=[[Kemps Film and TV Production Services Handbook]] |archive-date=April 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419223704/https://www.kftv.com/news/2024/03/12/wes-anderson-new-film-the-phoenician-scheme-shooting-germany |url-status=live }}</ref> The film was shot using [[Arricam]]s and an [[Arriflex 235]] with [[Kodak]] film stock. Color correction was done by Company3 UK.{{sfn|Rizov|2025|p=75}} Anderson, who avoids the usage of [[chroma key]], used an LED screen for the cloud footage outside the plane.{{sfn|Rizov|2025|p=77}}

French cinematographer [[Bruno Delbonnel]] shot on 35&nbsp;mm film, marking his first feature-length collaboration with Anderson.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Desowitz |first=Bill |date=2025-03-12 |title=20 Movies Shot on Film in 2025: Separate Safdie Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and More |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/2025-movies-shot-on-film-kodak-1235100813/ |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=IndieWire |language=en-US |archive-date=March 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250313011032/https://www.indiewire.com/features/craft/2025-movies-shot-on-film-kodak-1235100813/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This was the first live-action film to not be shot by his regular cinematographer [[Robert Yeoman]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharf |first=Zack |date=2018-01-09 |title=Robert Yeoman Looks Back on Filming Six Wes Anderson Films: 'We Always Find a Way of Pulling it Off' |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/robert-yeoman-wes-anderson-cinematographer-interview-grand-budapest-1201915576/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=IndieWire |language=en-US}}</ref> The film used the unusual 1.5:1 [[aspect ratio (image)|aspect ratio]].<ref name=":2" />

====Artwork====
[[File:Renoir - ENFANT ASSIS EN ROBE BLEUE, 1889 (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Pierre-Auguste Renoir]]'s ''Enfant Assis en Robe Bleue'' was loaned to the production.<ref name="nyt-zuckerman-25"/>]]
Anderson used several real-life paintings as props, including [[Pierre-Auguste Renoir|Renoir]]'s ''Enfant Assis en Robe Bleue'', once owned by [[Greta Garbo]], and [[René Magritte|Magritte]]'s ''The Equator'' from the collection of the [[Berlin State Museums]].<ref name="nyt-zuckerman-25">{{cite news |last1=Zuckerman |first1=Esther |title=In Wes Anderson's New Movie, Real Masterpieces Get a Starring Role |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/06/movies/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-masterpieces.html |access-date=10 June 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2025-06-06 |archive-date=June 11, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250611194814/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/06/movies/the-phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-masterpieces.html |url-status=live }}</ref> A few paintings from the [[Hamburger Kunsthalle]] also appear, among them one by [[Floris van Schooten]] and one by [[Juriaen Jacobsze]]. However, some of the paintings used in the film were replicas, including a [[Peter Paul Rubens|Rubens]].<ref name=":5" />

Jasper Sharp, a historian and curator at the [[Kunsthistorisches Museum]] in Vienna, curated and sourced the authentic artworks used in the film.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chen |first=Min |date=2025-05-21 |title=Yes, That's a Real Renoir in Wes Anderson's 'The Phoenician Scheme'—Here's How It Got There |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-art-curator-jasper-sharp-2647625 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Artnet News |language=en-US |archive-date=August 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250831160400/https://news.artnet.com/art-world/phoenician-scheme-wes-anderson-art-curator-jasper-sharp-2647625 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Release==
In February 2025, [[Focus Features]] acquired worldwide rights to the film, with its parent [[Universal Pictures]] handling international distribution.<ref name=":0"/> The film competed for the [[Palme d'Or]] at the [[2025 Cannes Film Festival]], where it had its world premiere on May 18.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cannes Film Festival Unveils 2025 Lineup|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|first1=Elsa|last1=Keslassy|first2=Ellise|last2=Shafer|date=10 April 2025|access-date=10 April 2025|url=https://variety.com/2025/film/festivals/cannes-film-festival-2025-lineup-1236364723/|archive-date=April 23, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423160915/https://variety.com/2025/film/festivals/cannes-film-festival-2025-lineup-1236364723/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Screenings Guide">{{cite web|url=https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/2025/the-screenings-guide-of-the-78th-festival-de-cannes/|title=The Screenings Guide of the 78th Festival de Cannes|date=8 May 2025|website=Festival de Cannes|access-date=8 May 2025|archive-date=May 8, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508200014/https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/2025/the-screenings-guide-of-the-78th-festival-de-cannes/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''The Phoenician Scheme'' was released theatrically in Germany by [[Universal Pictures]] on May 29, 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Phoenician Scheme |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/film/476624/ |access-date=7 June 2025 |website=[[Cineuropa]] |archive-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607092637/https://cineuropa.org/en/film/476624/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and had a limited theatrical release in the United States on May 30, 2025, before expanding nationwide on June 6, 2025.<ref name=":0"/>

== Reception ==
=== Box office ===
{{As of|2025|07|30|df=US}}, ''The Phoenician Scheme'' has grossed $20 million in the United States and Canada, and $19 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $39 million.<ref name=BOM />

=== Critical response ===
{{RT film|77|6.8|303|A caper made with all the intricacy of a [[Rube Goldberg machine]], ''The Phoenician Scheme'' doesn't deviate from Wes Anderson's increasingly ornate style but delivers the formula with mannered delicacy.|ref=y|access-date=October 28, 2025}} {{MC film|70|53|ref=y|access-date=June 28, 2025}} Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B-" on an A+ to F scale, while those surveyed by [[PostTrak]] gave it an 81% positive score, with 62% saying they would definitely recommend it.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/ |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=CinemaScore |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=2025-06-07 |title='Ballerina' Targeting $26M-$30M As 'Lilo & Stitch' Laughs To No. 1 With $32M-$34M – Friday PM Box Office Update |url=https://deadline.com/2025/06/box-office-ballerina-lilo-stitch-1236425576/ |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Tim Grierson of ''[[ScreenDaily]]'' wrote that while the film "is transporting", "the narrative proves to be fussy rather than delightful."<ref>{{Cite web|website=[[ScreenDaily]]|url=https://www.screendaily.com/reviews/the-phoenician-scheme-review-benicio-del-toro-and-wes-anderson-unite-for-espionage-comedy-drama/5204703.article|first=Tim|last=Grierson|date=18 May 2025|title='The Phoenician Scheme' review: Benicio del Toro and Wes Anderson unite for espionage comedy-drama|access-date=18 May 2025|archive-date=May 23, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523145824/https://www.screendaily.com/reviews/the-phoenician-scheme-review-benicio-del-toro-and-wes-anderson-unite-for-espionage-comedy-drama/5204703.article|url-status=live}}</ref> William Bibbiani of ''[[TheWrap]]'' declared the film "a serious work of art that plays like a [[boondoggle]]."<ref>{{Cite web|website=[[TheWrap]]|first=William|last=Bibbiani|title='The Phoenician Scheme' Review: Nobody Wes Andersons Like Wes Anderson|date=18 May 2025|access-date=18 May 2025|url=https://www.thewrap.com/the-phoenician-scheme-review-wes-anderson/}}</ref> Davide Abbatescianni of ''[[Cineuropa]]'' billed it "another elegant yet forgettable chapter in Anderson's filmography," which "ticks the boxes of visual and narrative quirkiness without delivering any substance."<ref>{{Cite web|website=[[Cineuropa]]|first=Davide|last=Abbatescianni|title=Review: The Phoenician Scheme|date=20 May 2025|access-date=5 June 2025|url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/477718//|archive-date=June 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250607040313/https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/477718//|url-status=live}}</ref>
